subject: Barinade
text: Throwing the Boomerang at Barinade until it penetrates the ring of fast moving Baris will stun him so the Baris can be destroyed.

evidence.quote: Keep throwing your Boomerang at Barinade until it can penetrate the fast moving Baris, and it will stun him.  Destroy the Baris.

subject: Barinade
text: While destroying the Baris, be careful because the satellite dishes will resume their attacking.

evidence.quote: Be careful while destroying them, as the "satellite dishes" will resume their attacking.

subject: Barinade
text: In the final phase once all Baris are dead, stun Barinade with the Boomerang and strike its base with Jump Attacks while watching out for satellite dishes firing.

evidence.quote: Once all of the Baris are dead, then you enter the boss' final phase, in which you are finally able to damage him.  Stun him with your Boomerang, then run into strike it's base with Jump Attacks.  Watch out, however - the satellite dishes will keep on firing the whole time.

subject: Barinade
text: Barinade retreats into the ground briefly after two Jump Attacks and will be defeated after five Jump Attacks.

evidence.quote: After two Jump Attacks, Barinade will retreat into the ground briefly. ... After five Jump Attacks, Barinade will be defeated.

subject: Phantom Ganon
text: To damage Phantom Ganon in the first phase, shoot him with an arrow as he emerges from the painting that appears slightly brighter.

evidence.quote: To damage Phantom Ganon in this phase, you must shoot him with an arrow as he emerges from the painting.  The real Phantom Ganon will make the painting slightly brighter.

subject: Phantom Ganon
text: When Phantom Ganon charges down two paintings on a flying horse, the fake Ganon turns back at the last minute while the real one emerges and scatters the field with electricity.

evidence.quote: At the start of the fight, Phantom Ganon will be mounted on a flying horse, and will retreat into one of the paintings that encircle the room.  He will then appear in two of the paintings, charging towards you down the path; one of them is the real Phantom Ganon, the other is fake.  The fake one will turn back at the last minute, the real one will emerge from the painting and scatter the field with electricity.

subject: Phantom Ganon
text: After being shot three times in the first phase, Phantom Ganon enters his second phase where the Shield is worthless and switching to the Biggoron Sword provides a wider reach advantage.

evidence.quote: After you have shot Phantom Ganon three times in his first phase, then he will enter his second phase.  If you have the Biggoron Sword, then switch to it now.  The Shield is worthless in this phase, and the Biggoron Sword's wider reach is a significant advantage in this next part.

subject: Phantom Ganon
text: To damage Phantom Ganon in his second phase, stun him by reflecting his lightning balls back at him using sword strikes or Bottles as the ball accelerates with each successive hit.

evidence.quote: Phantom Ganon will now begin throwing balls of lightning at you.  To damage him now, you must stun him by reflecting these lightning balls back at him using sword strikes (if you're feeling silly, you can also use Bottles).  The ball moves faster with each successive hit.

subject: Phantom Ganon
text: Standing on the opposite end of the field to reflect lightning shots is easier and recommended for newer players, while standing closer makes reflection harder but finishes the fight faster.

evidence.quote: If you're feeling reckless, then you can stand closer to Phantom Ganon.  This makes it harder to reflect shots, but can get the fight over faster if you're good.  Conversely, you can stand on the opposite end of the field to reflect the shots.  This is easier, and recommended for newer or uncoordinated players.

subject: Phantom Ganon
text: When Phantom Ganon is stunned and falls to the ground, execute one Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or Master Sword followed by regular strikes.

evidence.quote: Once the ball strikes Phantom Ganon, then he will be stunned briefly and fall to the ground.  At this point, you should run in and begin pummeling him to death with the Biggoron Sword (or Master Sword if you don't have the Biggoron Sword yet).  Only do one Jump Attack, then proceed to regular strikes.

subject: Volvagia
text: To begin the fight against Volvagia, jump out to the large slab of rock in the middle of the cavern and run to the middle of the platform.

evidence.quote: Jump out to the large slab of rock in the middle of the cavern, and run to the middle of the platform to begin the fight.

subject: Volvagia
text: In Volvagia's first phase, he emerges from one of nine pits marked by smoke and cinders, where striking his head with a Megaton Hammer Jump Attack will stun him.

evidence.quote: In Volvagia's first phase, he appears randomly in one of the nine pits that dot the battlefield.  You'll know which pit he'll appear in, as a large amount of smoke and cinders will appear around the pit.  Run towards this pit, and Volvagia's head will emerge.  Smash his head with the Megaton Hammer (use a Jump Attack with the Megaton Hammer for best results), and it will briefly stun Volvagia.

subject: Volvagia
text: Once Volvagia is stunned in his first phase, follow up with a Jump Attack using the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer.

evidence.quote: At this point, you can get one more attack in on him.  So make it a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword for best results (if you don't have the Biggoron Sword, then the Megaton Hammer is a decent substitute).

subject: Volvagia
text: In his second phase when Volvagia flies around breathing fire, avoid damage by running continuously in a small circle near the center of the battlefield.

evidence.quote: In his second phase, Volvagia will emerge from one of the pits (again, you can tell which ones by the smoke and cinders that appear around the pit) and fly around the room, chasing you and trying to breath fire on you.  The easiest way to avoid damage in this phase is to just run continuously to the left or right in a small circle, preferably near the center of the battlefield.

subject: Volvagia
text: When Volvagia flies toward the ceiling causing boulders to rain down, run to the edge of the battlefield and hang off the edge to avoid the attack.

evidence.quote: After you damage Volvagia again, then he will emerge from the pits once more and begin flying towards the ceiling.  The roof will begin to fall, raining the battlefield with boulders.  Easily the best way to avoid this form of attack is to just run to the edge of the battlefield and hang off the edge.

subject: Morpha
text: A single attack from Morpha deals four to six hearts of damage.

evidence.quote: The only thing "hard" about Morpha is it's ability to deal quite a large amount of damage in one attack (which deal four to six hearts of damage... but since you should have fourteen or fifteen heart containers by now, that's no big deal).

subject: Morpha
text: Avoid entering the water or standing on the four inner platforms; remain on the room's perimeter, using the middle platform ladders if you fall into the water.

evidence.quote: For the duration of this boss fight, it's very important that you avoid entering the water, since this will give the boss easy opportunity to attack you.  You should also avoid standing on the four platforms on the inside of the room, since this will allow Morpha to attack you from several sides ... If you fall in the water or somehow end up on one of the inner platforms, then get back to the perimeter of the room posthaste.  There are ladders on the platforms in the middle of the room you can climb up if you happen to fall in the water.

subject: Morpha
text: When Morpha spins rapidly in the water, it generates tentacle arms that grab and hurl you into the wall upon contact, but the Longshot outranges them.

evidence.quote: Morpha's "nucleus" (the large white brain/eye) will typically enter one of these arms, and the arm will stretch out towards you.  If you make contact with the arm, then it will grab you and hurl you into the wall. ... Thankfully, your Longshot outranges Morpha's arms by a considerable distance.  So stay a fair distance away to avoid Morpha's only attack - it's arms.  You'll know Morpha is generating another arm and is getting ready to attack when it spins around rapidly in the water below.

subject: Morpha
text: When Morpha's nucleus enters an arm, grab it with the Longshot to stun it and perform a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer before it bounces back into the water.

evidence.quote: When Morpha enters one of it's arms, this is your opportunity to attack.  Grab it with the Longshot, and it will remained stunned long enough for you to attack it once, maybe twice.  Which is why you should make that attack a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword (which you can, and should, have by now, no excuses).  If you don't have the Biggoron's Sword, then a Jump Attack with the Megaton Hammer will do.  After Morpha is damaged, it will bounce randomly around the room for a little while, then return to the water and start spawning more arms.

subject: Bongo Bongo
text: Drop down the pit in the middle of the room to begin the boss fight against Bongo Bongo.

evidence.quote: Drop down the pit in the middle of the room to begin the fight.

subject: Bongo Bongo
text: Equip the Kokiri Boots to avoid making the fight unnecessarily difficult while dodging Bongo Bongo's hand attacks and drum pounds.

evidence.quote: The entire boss fight is fought on a giant drum.  A giant Bongo Drum.  Yep, that's right.  Bongo Bongo will attack you with his hands, or try to knock you off the drum by pounding it hard.  Just use basic dodging to avoid these attacks. ... Just make sure you're using the Kokiri Boots, otherwise this fight will be unnecessarily difficult.

subject: Bongo Bongo
text: Z-Target and shoot both hands with arrows to stun them, then use the Lens of Truth to spot Bongo Bongo's eye, shoot it with an arrow, and Jump Attack his fallen torso with the Biggoron Sword.

evidence.quote: To damage Bongo Bongo, you must make his eye appear.  To do this, shoot both of his hands with arrows to stun them.  They recover quickly, so shoot fast.  Use Z-Targeting; the hands move much too fast, and the constant movement of the drum makes manual aiming pretty much impossible.  Once you stun both hands, use the Lens of Truth to look at the space between the hands, and you'll see Bongo Bongo's eye.  Shoot it with an Arrow as well, and Bongo Bongo's torso will fall to the floor, letting you attack it.  As always, that attack should be a Jump Attack from the Biggoron Sword (which you can, and should, have by now).

subject: Bongo Bongo
text: Stunning Bongo Bongo's hands causes them to drop magic and arrows if you run low.

evidence.quote: If you run low on magic or arrows, Bongo Bongo's hands drop more when you stun them.

subject: Twinrova
text: The Sorceress Sisters have opposing elements: Kotake is Ice, and Koume is Fire.

evidence.quote: The Sisters each have their own element which opposes the other.  Kotake is Ice, and Koume is Fire.

subject: Twinrova
text: In the first phase, keep both sisters in view without Z-Targeting and use the Mirror Shield to reflect one sister's elemental magic beam into the opposing sister, as missing creates a damaging floor ring.

evidence.quote: You have to now use the Mirror Shield to reflect this beam into the other sister, much as you reflected the beams of light earlier in the dungeon. ... Don't even TRY to Z-Target to aim the beam; if you do, the beam will just fire off in some random direction and won't even get near the other sister. ... If you fail to reflect one of the beams, then it will impact on the floor, creating a ring that damages you (and in the case of Kotake's ice beam, freezes you... which sucks).

subject: Twinrova
text: To stun Twinrova and make her vulnerable to attack, you must absorb three spells of the same alignment in a row with your shield, as absorbing an opposing element negates prior charges.

evidence.quote: In order to stun Twinrova and make her vulnerable to attack, you have to absorb three spells of the same alignment IN A ROW.  This means that, if you absorb two fire spells, then an ice spell, then the two fires will be negated and you have to absorb two more ice spells.

subject: Twinrova
text: Twinrova indicates which beam she will use by waving her right wand for Ice and left wand for Fire, while the Mirror Shield flashes red for fire and white for ice, flashing faster as more beams are absorbed.

evidence.quote: You can tell which beam Twinrova is about to use by looking at which wand she waves - the right is Ice, the left is Fire.  You can also tell which beams your Mirror Shield has absorbed by looking at it - it flashes red for fire, and white for ice.  The faster it flashes, the more beams absorbed.

subject: Twinrova
text: After absorbing three consecutive beams, keep the Mirror Shield drawn to fire a beam that stuns Twinrova, then equip Hover Boots, Jump Attack across the gap, strike her with your sword, and switch back to Kokiri Boots on the main platform.

evidence.quote: After you absorb three beams of the same alignment in a row, then the Mirror Shield will unleash a massive beam back at Twinrova (keep the shield drawn to make sure the beam connects).  This will stun her momentarily, causing her to fall to the platform below her.  At this point, quickly equip the Hover Boots and draw your sword.  Run out to Twinrova.  When you're halfway across the gap, use a Jump Attack to go the rest of the way and damage Twinrova at the same time.  Then switch to basic sword strikes.  When Twinrova recovers, return to the main platform and switch back to the Kokiri Boots, where the second phase starts over.

subject: Ganondorf
text: Navi cannot Z-Target Ganondorf or provide C-Up advice until he is stunned with a Light Arrow, and she becomes unavailable again when he recovers.

evidence.quote: Navi is unavailable during this fight, meaning you can't Z-Target and she can't give you advice with C-Up.  Once Ganondorf is stunned with a Light Arrow, then Navi can Z-Target again, but Navi becomes unavailable once more when Ganondorf recovers.

subject: Ganondorf
text: Ganondorf remains stationary in the center of the room and performs a Shockwave attack that collapses floor pieces into pits leading down to Tower Floor Five if approached before he is stunned.

evidence.quote: For one, Ganondorf remains stationary in the center of the room.  He also has a Shockwave attack, which will collapse bits of the floor, creating pits that lead back down to the Tower Floor Five area.  For this reason, don't go near Ganondorf until he is stunned, or else he will use the Shockwave and make this fight more difficult then it needs to be.

subject: Ganondorf
text: Reflect Ganondorf's balls of lightning back at him with sword strikes or Empty Bottles, as any missed lightning ball will destroy the floor panel you are standing on.

evidence.quote: Ganondorf will throw balls of lightning at you, which you must reflect back at him with sword strikes (or you can use Empty Bottles if you're feeling creative).  If you miss a ball of lightning and it doesn't hit you, then it will destroy whatever floor panel you happen to be standing on, knocking you down to a lower floor.

subject: Ganondorf
text: If knocked down to the lower floor during the fight with Ganondorf, climb back up using the tiles on the pillar in the middle of the room.

evidence.quote: If you miss a ball of lightning and it doesn't hit you, then it will destroy whatever floor panel you happen to be standing on, knocking you down to a lower floor.  You'll have to climb back up using the tiles on the pillar in the middle of the room.

subject: Twinrova
text: When the sisters merge into Twinrova, players can Z-Target and use the Biggoron Sword, keeping it put away until ready to damage Twinrova, or use the Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
Now truly Twinrova, the Sorceress Sisters form one entity.  So you can now Z-
Target.  If you have the Biggoron Sword (which you can, and should, have by
now), then use it for this stage of the fight, but keep it "Put Away" until
you're ready to damage Twinrova. ... If all of this
is too much for you, just use the Master Sword
